history.because: the cognitive contracts were wired into the runtime health surface: two health fragments and one boot import, which is the edge that makes contract_health and growth_report reachable from a live report rather than only from tests. 215 kernel lines and one cross-package edge for the thing that says whether any of the contracts are load-bearing.

two lines: the registration moved from core/runtime/foundations into core/cognition/cognitive_integration_layer, because a foundation may not reach into cognition. The subsystem publishes and the surface asks, which is the direction memory_facade already uses.

36 lines in core/runtime/health_fragments.py: the reset now returns what it removed and a context manager puts it back, because a clear-only reset was permanent for the process and left every later test finding an empty register.

31 lines across three intent and validation modules: a capability-question guard in desktop_objective_intent, a wh-question guard in skill_task_bridge, and the claim that model_validation had a test for and nobody had registered.

109 lines in core/conversation/response_reliability.py: a structured-payload check so the prose leak detector stops rejecting a well-formed JSON extraction for mentioning the user it was asked to extract.
